jp: あれ、このシャツ、値札[ねふだ]{が/は|ga-existence}ついたまま{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: Hey, this shirt still has the price tag on it!
why: Noticing something surprising right in front of you is voiced with じゃないか; かな and っけ do not exclaim.

jp: 見[み]て、この野菜[やさい]、昨日[きのう]{より|yori-comparison}ずっと安[やす]い{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: Look, these vegetables are much cheaper than yesterday!
why: The speaker points out a surprising fact the listener can see for themselves; かな, っけ and かも do not carry that exclamation.

jp: 財布[さいふ]{の|no-possessive}中[なか]{が/は|ga-subject}空[から]っぽ{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: Hey, my wallet is empty!
why: A sudden discovery of what is plainly there takes じゃないか; かな and かも would only wonder or guess.

jp: このコーヒー、三千円[さんぜんえん]{も|mo-emphasis}する{じゃないか|janai-ka}。

jp: 買[か]い物[もの]{に|ni-purpose}行[い]く{と|to-quote}言[い]った{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: I told you I was going shopping!

jp: ほら、ここ{に|ni-location}値引[ねび]き{の|no-possessive}シール{が|ga-subject}貼[は]ってある{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: Look, there's a discount sticker stuck right here!

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}給料日[きゅうりょうび]{じゃないか|janai-ka}。おいしい物[もの]{を|o-object}食[た]べ{に|ni-purpose}行[い]こう。
en: Today is payday! Let's go out for something nice to eat.
why: The speaker has just realised a happy fact and exclaims with じゃないか; かな and っけ would make the date a puzzle.

jp: 君[きみ]{が/は|ga-subject}払[はら]う{と|to-quote}言[い]った{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: You said you'd pay!
why: Throwing the listener's own words back at them takes じゃないか; かな and っけ would not hold them to it.

jp: この店[みせ]{の|no-possessive}カレー、意外[いがい]とおいしい{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: Hey, the curry at this place is surprisingly good!
why: A pleasantly surprised discovery is voiced with じゃないか; かな and かも would only guess at the taste.

jp: みんな{で|de-scope}割[わ]り勘[かん]{に|ni-change}しよう{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: Let's all split the bill.
why: After the volitional form, じゃないか makes a hearty proposal to a group; かな would turn it into a private musing.

jp: せっかく{の|no-possessive}セールだ。思[おも]い切[き]って新[あたら]しい冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]{を|o-object}買[か]おう{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: It's a sale, after all. Let's go for it and buy a new fridge!
why: Volitional plus じゃないか rallies the listener to act together; かな would make it a private musing, and っけ and かも cannot follow the volitional.

jp: ネット{で|de-means}買[か]ったほう{が|ga-subject}安[やす]かった{んじゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: Wouldn't it have been cheaper to buy it online?

jp: もう少[すこ]し待[ま]て{ば|ba-conditional}、値段[ねだん]{が|ga-subject}下[さ]がる{んじゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: If we wait a little longer, I think the price will drop, don't you?
why: The speaker puts forward a guess and invites agreement with んじゃないか; んだっけ would ask for recall instead.

jp: その傘[かさ]、昨日[きのう]コンビニ{で|de-place}買[か]った{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: You bought that umbrella at the convenience store yesterday, remember?
why: Calling up a shared fact the listener should know takes じゃないか; っけ would mean the speaker is the one who forgot.

jp: ここ{の|no-possessive}パン{は|wa-topic}安[やす]い{じゃないですか|janai-ka}。だから毎日[まいにち]混[こ]んでいる{んです|no-explanatory}。
en: The bread here is cheap, you know. That's why it's crowded every day.
why: Polite じゃないですか reminds the listener of a fact they know and sets up the reason; ですっけ and ですかね would doubt the fact.

jp: 冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]{の|no-possessive}中[なか]、牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{が/は|ga-existence}ない{じゃないか|janai-ka}。

jp: スーパー{は|wa-topic}もう閉[し]まっている{じゃないか|janai-ka}。

jp: この店[みせ]{は|wa-topic}カード{が/を|potential-ga}使[つか]えない{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
en: Hey, this shop doesn't take cards!

jp: 通帳[つうちょう]{を|o-object}見[み]た{ら|tara-conditional}、お金[かね]{が/は|ga-subject}ほとんど残[のこ]っていない{じゃないか|janai-ka}。

jp: 君[きみ]{は|wa-topic}さっき{から|kara-from}何[なに]{も|mo-total-negation}食[た]べていない{じゃないか|janai-ka}。
